title: Tech Note: Synchronizing an HTTP client with 4D Server v12
author: Christophe Keromen, CKTI Consulting Firm

historical_commentary.text: Adobe AIR has been effectively abandoned as a client platform for years (Adobe stopped its own investment and it never gained broad mobile traction), so the specific AIR-based client in this note is no longer a realistic implementation choice. 4D's own v12 table-level replication mechanism has also been superseded conceptually by later synchronization/offline strategies and by REST/ORDA-based data access, which modern clients (web, native mobile, or Qodly-built apps) use instead of a custom AIR client talking to a proprietary sync protocol.
related_updates: REST APIs built on ORDA (4D v16 R5+) as the modern way to build synchronized/offline-capable clients, replacing both Adobe AIR and the classic table-level replication approach
Qodly Studio for building modern web/mobile front-ends against a 4D backend
